transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. This is a gas safety issue, so I cannot advise on internal repairs or part replacement. However, this symptom (flame lights but dies when you release the knob) is very commonly caused by the flame-failure device not getting hot enough because the burner cap is slightly misaligned, wet, or dirty from recent cleaning. Before calling an engineer, please ensure the oven is off and cool, then check that the burner cap sits perfectly flat and dry. If it looks correct but the problem persists, you will need a Gas Safe registered engineer to inspect the thermocouple and gas valve.

Thanks. I can't see anything out of place with the burner, and I've held the knob in for up to 30 seconds with no luck. There's also some burnt-on fat around the base of the burner. Is that worth cleaning, or should I just get an engineer?

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. Yes, please clean it. Grease and fat can insulate the thermocouple (the safety probe), preventing it from getting hot enough to keep the gas valve open. Once cool, carefully remove any burnt-on residue from around the burner base and ensure the flame holes are clear. Because these involve sealed gas components, I cannot advise on their replacement; please call a Gas Safe registered engineer to fix it.
